title: Agility: は and の as light, quick tools
summary: Japanese can make a topic (は) or box up a whole clause (の) with almost no effort, so sentences use them where English would feel heavy.

blocks.text: Languages differ in **agility**: how light and fast a tool is to use. A tool that is heavy in English may be nimble in Japanese, so Japanese uses it all the time. If you do not notice this, ordinary sentences feel odd.
は: a topic in one step

English "speaking of …" or "as for …" is clumsy, so you use it rarely. Japanese **は** is tiny, so it can be dropped in wherever you want to **set one thing against another**. The comment after a は topic is always a complete logical clause (lesson 60), and the new topic says: "what I say next may differ from what I said about the neighbor".

blocks.jp: この店はラーメンはおいしいが、カレーはまずい。
blocks.en: At this shop the ramen is good, but the curry is bad.

blocks.text: Here the clause carries two sub-topics. Each は contrasts: ramen against curry. If the comment is the same, use **も** instead.
の: a whole clause in a noun box

The **nominalizing の** is a pronoun that bundles everything before it into a single noun, "the one that …". English needs preparation for "what she saw when she opened the door was …", but Japanese slips it in anywhere, even as a topic.
朝の町に響くのは鐘だ。 What resounds in the morning town is a bell.
So 朝の町に響くのは鐘だ is not "a bell resounds". It is an A-is-B sentence: A is "the one that resounds in the morning town" (topic), B is "a bell".

blocks.jp: 彼女が部屋で見たのは、古い人形だった。
blocks.en: What she saw in the room was an old doll.

blocks.jp: 毎朝歩くのは気持ちがいい。

items: **Agility** = how light a tool is. は and の are very light in Japanese.
**は** can be used again and again to set topics against each other; **も** says the comment is the same.
**の** turns a clause into a noun, "the one that …".
In a sentence like Xのは Y だ, X is the topic and Y is the answer.

options: How light and quick a tool is to use in a language

questions.instruction: Why does は feel heavy in English?
options: "Speaking of ..." is a clumsy way to set a topic
questions.note: Japanese は is a small particle, so it is used freely.

questions.instruction: Fill the gap to say the ramen is good but the curry is bad
questions.prompt: ラーメン＿＿おいしいが、カレーはまずい。

questions.instruction: Which particle says the comment is the same as for another topic?
Tap the pronoun-like word that boxes the clause
questions.note: の turns what is before it into "the one that".

questions.prompt: 窓から見えるのは海だ。
options: What can be seen from the window is the sea
The window is seen by me
I see the sea from far away

questions.instruction: In 昨日買ったのは赤い靴だ, what is the topic?
questions.note: 昨日買ったの is boxed into a noun and marked with は.

questions.prompt: Xのは Y だ is an A-is-B sentence.
questions.note: A = the boxed thing, B = Y + だ.

questions.instruction: Which sentence uses の as a noun box?
questions.note: 歩く + の makes the activity into a noun.

questions.prompt: What I wanted was a new bag.
questions.note: The boxed topic, then the modified noun and the copula.

questions.instruction: What does the comment after a は topic have to be?
questions.note: It needs its own carriage and engine.

questions.instruction: Pick the best reading of アフリカはライオンはいるがトラはいない
options: In Africa, lions exist but tigers do not
Africa is a lion and a tiger
Lions and tigers are in Africa
questions.note: Two contrasting sub-topics inside the Africa topic.
